options: more than enough
carefully rationed
adequate
steady
questions.explanation: Adequate is the trap, since it means just enough. A supply that would serve twice the crew is ample, which means generously beyond what is needed.

questions.stem: a courteous reply
options: polite
prompt
brief
formal
questions.explanation: Courteous refers to good manners. A reply can be prompt, formal or brief without being courteous.

questions.stem: to conceal the damage
options: repair
exaggerate
report
hide
questions.explanation: Conceal means to keep out of sight. Exaggerating or reporting the damage both draw attention to it instead.

questions.stem: a feeble excuse
options: frail
rude
hurried
unconvincing
questions.explanation: Frail is the everyday sense of feeble applied to a body; applied to an excuse, feeble means weak in the sense of unconvincing.

questions.stem: to postpone the ceremony
options: cut short
put off
hurry through
call off
questions.explanation: To postpone is to move an event to a later time; calling it off cancels it altogether.

questions.stem: a prudent investor
options: wealthy
fortunate
sensible
timid
questions.explanation: Timid is close but not right: a prudent investor uses good judgment, which sometimes means acting boldly.

questions.stem: obsolete equipment
options: borrowed
broken
out of date
expensive
questions.explanation: Obsolete equipment may still work perfectly; it has simply been replaced by something newer.

questions.stem: to verify the report
options: summarize
question
publish
confirm
questions.explanation: Verify means to check something and establish that it is true, which is the opposite of merely questioning it.

questions.stem: a somber mood
options: tense
restless
hopeful
gloomy
questions.explanation: Somber is specifically dark and serious; tense and restless are unpleasant moods of a different kind.

questions.stem: to relinquish the title
options: give up
hand down
take back
compete for
questions.explanation: To relinquish is to surrender something you hold. Hand down suggests passing it to an heir, which is a different act.

questions.stem: a benevolent ruler
options: wealthy
strict
kindly
powerful
questions.explanation: Benevolent describes goodwill toward others, not the amount of power or money a ruler has.

questions.stem: a novice sailor
options: occasional
fearless
careless
beginning
questions.explanation: Occasional is the near miss: a novice is new to the activity, which is about experience rather than how often the person sails.

questions.stem: to ponder an offer
options: think over
mention
refuse
accept
questions.explanation: To ponder is to consider carefully; accepting or refusing comes after the pondering is done.

questions.stem: to deter trespassers
options: warn
discourage
identify
punish
questions.explanation: Deter means to prevent an action by making it unappealing. Warning and punishing are methods that may deter, not the meaning itself.

questions.stem: a resilient community
options: rapidly growing
closely knit
well funded
quick to recover
questions.explanation: Resilient describes the ability to bounce back after hardship, which a community can have whether or not it is wealthy or close.

questions.stem: a plausible excuse
options: detailed
familiar
truthful
believable
questions.explanation: Truthful is the trap: a plausible excuse sounds believable, and it may still be a lie.

questions.stem: a meticulous record
options: unusually long
painstakingly careful
neatly typed
strictly private
questions.explanation: Meticulous refers to attention to every detail; length and neatness are not the same thing.

questions.stem: an obstinate child
options: bashful
spoiled
stubborn
restless
questions.explanation: Obstinate means refusing to change one's mind. Spoiled is a common companion trait but describes upbringing, not stubbornness.

questions.stem: a tranquil evening
options: dull
peaceful
chilly
lonely
questions.explanation: Tranquil means calm and untroubled; dull adds a negative judgment that tranquil does not carry.

questions.stem: a vigilant guard
options: armed
patient
strict
watchful
questions.explanation: Vigilant means alert to danger. A guard may be strict or patient without being vigilant.

questions.stem: indifferent to the criticism
options: grateful for
puzzled by
unconcerned about
angered by
questions.explanation: Indifferent means simply not caring one way or the other, which is a milder reaction than being angered or puzzled.

questions.stem: a remote possibility that anyone was hurt
options: far away
slight
alarming
growing
questions.explanation: Far away is the trap drawn from the everyday sense of remote. Applied to a possibility, remote means very unlikely.

questions.stem: to ridicule the plan
options: revise
doubt
make fun of
reject
questions.explanation: Ridicule adds mockery to disapproval; a person can doubt or reject a plan while treating it seriously.

questions.stem: seldom absent from practice
options: briefly
never
rarely
willingly
questions.explanation: Never is the tempting choice, but seldom allows for a few absences.

questions.stem: to tarnish a reputation
options: damage
reveal
exaggerate
dispute
questions.explanation: Tarnish literally describes metal losing its shine; applied to a reputation it means to damage it, not merely to argue about it.

questions.stem: a drastic change in policy
options: extreme
permanent
unpopular
sudden
questions.explanation: Sudden is the near miss: drastic describes how far-reaching the change is, not how quickly it arrives.

questions.stem: a rash promise
options: broken
generous
bold
hasty
questions.explanation: Here rash has nothing to do with skin: it means made without thinking. Bold is close but lacks the sense of carelessness.

questions.stem: a quaint village
options: unusually small
charmingly old-fashioned
poorly kept
newly built
questions.explanation: Quaint carries approval for something pleasingly old-fashioned; small alone does not make a village quaint.

questions.stem: the supplies dwindled
options: steadily decreased
were divided up
suddenly vanished
were spoiled
questions.explanation: Dwindle describes a gradual shrinking, so a sudden disappearance is not it.

questions.stem: a sharp retort
options: gesture
tone of voice
quick reply
criticism
questions.explanation: A retort is an answer given back to someone. It is often critical, but the word itself means the reply.

questions.stem: a gaunt face
options: pale and freckled
thin and drawn
stern and angry
round and full
questions.explanation: Gaunt describes thinness from hunger, illness or exhaustion rather than an expression.

questions.stem: a keen observer of small details
options: patient
sharp-eyed
eager
quiet
questions.explanation: Eager is the everyday sense of keen, but a keen observer is one who notices what others miss. Patience may help such a person, though it is not what the word means.

questions.stem: to coax the cat from under the porch
options: firmly command
gently persuade
carefully lift
slowly chase
questions.explanation: Coaxing works by patient encouragement, so commanding and chasing are both too forceful.

questions.stem: to quench the flames
options: spread
contain
put out
satisfy
questions.explanation: Satisfy comes from quenching a thirst; with flames the word means to extinguish them, and containing a fire is not the same as putting it out.

questions.stem: to vex the substitute teacher
options: defy
confuse
annoy
interrupt
questions.explanation: Vex means to irritate. Interrupting or defying may cause irritation, but neither is the meaning of the word.

questions.stem: to feign surprise
options: exaggerate
pretend
admit
overcome
questions.explanation: Exaggerate is the near miss: to feign surprise is to fake a feeling you do not have at all.
